query: What signals suggest an expense will be declined?

per_column.name: asset_form_factor
per_column.rationale: Type of asset being expensed is knowable at submission and plausibly correlates with decline rates (e.g., premium hardware vs. accessories); a legitimate external predictor.

per_column.name: asset_vendor
per_column.rationale: Vendor is known pre-decision and may carry signal (approved vendor lists, cost profiles), so a valid predictor of decline.

per_column.name: is_premium_or_nonstandard_asset
per_column.rationale: Non-standard/premium items are plausibly more likely to be declined; known at submission and outside the focus, hence a strong candidate predictor.

per_column.name: is_travel_related
per_column.rationale: Whether the expense is travel-related is known upfront and category-level decline patterns are plausible; legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: Presence of a source_id is a metadata/completeness indicator available at submission; missing linkage could plausibly raise decline likelihood. Valid predictor, though risk of proxying process state is mild.

per_column.name: has_processed_date
per_column.rationale: processed_date is populated as part of processing the expense to its final state; its presence is largely determined by the outcome workflow and only known after adjudication, making it post-outcome leakage rather than a pre-decision signal.

per_column.name: description_specificity
per_column.rationale: Quality/specificity of the description is known at submission and vague requests plausibly get declined more; a genuine external predictor.

per_column.name: ci_identifier_quality
per_column.rationale: Quality of the configuration-item identifier is submission-time metadata; poor identification could raise decline risk. Legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: submitting_department
per_column.rationale: Department is known before adjudication and decline rates plausibly vary by department; valid predictor (partially overlaps existing 'department' column, but framed as submitting department).

judge.rationale: Most added columns are submission-time attributes of the expense (asset type, vendor, premium flag, travel flag, description/CI quality, department) that lie outside the focus and plausibly carry predictive signal about decline, giving the set solid predictive leverage. 'has_processed_date' is flagged as leakage because processed_date presence is driven by the adjudication workflow and known only after the outcome. 'submitting_department' partially duplicates an existing column, slightly limiting incremental gain. Overall a coherent, mostly legitimate feature set with moderate-to-good utility.
